title: FOR STUDENTS, ANYTHING GOES
text:
The cast and crew of North Kingstown High School students who will be performing in the Tony Award-winning musical “Anything Goes” will feature a healthy dose of Jamestown residents.
With music and lyrics by Cole Porter, “Anything Goes” debuted on Broadway in 1934. The classical musical now sails to North Kingstown with a cast of charismatic characters aboard an ocean liner traveling from New York to London with a cargo of high-energy musical numbers.
Heading up the raucous crew is Jamestown’s Cal Mooney, as the ship’s captain, who is always on the lookout for celebrity guests to liven up the scene onboard. Mooney, 16, has performed with the Jamestown Community Theatre, including “Matilda” and “Nunsense” in 2025, and is relishing the opportunity to flex her singing, dancing and, especially, comedy chops.
“It’s a different type of humor,”
Mooney said. “It’s the 1930s so a lot of the jokes are a bit older, but that just broadens the audience, I think, because there are going to be a lot of older people seeing the show. They’ll find it funny.”
It’s not only about the comedy for Mooney, however.
“I really like Cole Porter songs,” she said.
As much fun as the funniest bits are, Mooney also is throwing herself into the big dance numbers, such as the namesake finale, “Anything Goes.” The showstopper calls for the full cast to don their tapping shoes and bring the house down. And in the North Kingstown version, they do just that.
“This show especially has really pushed my dance abilities, and I feel like I’ve improved tremendously in that aspect,” Mooney said.
The full cast participated in a “tap boot camp” a week before rehearsals started, so they could get that final number just right. The extra practice helped, with the experience sparking further interest in the dance form for Mooney.
“I knew nothing about tap before the show,” she said. “The first time I’d ever tapped was at boot camp. But I actually ended up really, really liking it, which surprised me.”
Jamestown junior Maddie Raymond enjoyed the old-time feel of the musical that’s been around nearly a century, proving that the story stands the test of time. As one of four angels, she was thrilled to learn so much choreography. She usually focuses on singing in musicals, but relished the chance to try out her dancing skills in a production that heavily emphasizes that aspect.
“In the past, I’ve been cast in more singing roles, and now I’ve had the opportunity to do basically all dancing,” Raymond said. “So, the experience has been very fun, and I was very excited to be an angel.”
For Raymond, community and camaraderie were the most rewarding aspects of the production.
“Most of my friends are in the musical, and I think it’s really nice that I could just be with them doing something fun after school,” she said.
It’s not all fun, however. “Sometimes the 12-hour days are rough,” Raymond added.
Jamestown senior Olivia Rohrbach plays the musical’s lead, Hope Harcourt, a sophisticated young debutante. In her role, Rohrbach, who starred with Mooney in North Kingstown’s 2025 production of “Legally Blonde,” said she is imbuing her character with elegance and confidence. She also likes the refined dresses she gets to wear in the heiress role.
“I lucked out with my costumes,” she said.
Rohrback said she especially likes singing “It’s De-Lovely,” which was used by Chrysler in advertising DeSoto automobiles.
“I like singing it,” she said. “It’s fun to sing. And I think it’s pretty catchy.”
Also in the cast from Jamestown are Mairead Lapierre, Maggie Reed, Anne Smith and Ruby Starr. Crewmembers from Jamestown are Kathryn Borges, Magnus Moorehead, Abigail Brodin, Isabella Soucy, Flannery Freeman and Hayden Rosa. Jack Charest is in the pit orchestra.
If you want to go:
WHAT: North Kingstown High School’s production of “Anything Goes”
WHEN: 7 p.m. Friday, March 6, 2 p.m. and 7 p.m. Saturday, March 7, and 2 p.m. Sunday, March 8
WHERE: North Kingstown High School, 150 Fairway Drive
ADMISSION: $20
